clips.send: Fort McPherson. Today: Tyler Perry Studios, Atlanta. An Army post in southwest Atlanta for more than 120 years; in World War I it held German prisoners of war. After it closed in 2011, much of the land became Tyler Perry Studios.

clips.send: Yingtian. Today: Nanjing, Jiangsu. Zhu Yuanzhang founded the Ming at Yingtian and built a city wall over 35 km long — much of it still stands. In 1421 the capital moved to Beijing.

clips.send: Warm Springs. Spring water comes out of the ground here at about 88 degrees Fahrenheit (31 degrees Celsius ). Franklin D. Roosevelt first came in 1924 hoping the warm pools would help his legs after polio, built his Little White House here, and died here on April 12, 1945; nearby FDR State Park was built by the CCC.

clips.send: Chibi (Red Cliffs). Today: northwest of Chibi City, Hubei (one view). Sun Quan and Liu Bei’s allies set fire to Cao Cao’s chained ships on the Yangtze. This battle led to the Three Kingdoms.

clips.send: Gadsden Purchase. Today: southern Arizona and New Mexico. In 1853 the US paid Mexico $10 million for this strip of desert south of the Gila River, because it offered the flattest route for a railroad to California. It completed the outline of the lower 48 states.

clips.send: Trinity site. Today: White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico. At 5:29 a.m. on 16 July 1945, Manhattan Project scientists exploded the first atomic bomb in this New Mexico desert. The flash lit up the sky for many miles around, and the heat melted the sand into a green glass now called trinitite. The site is open to visitors only on a few days a year.

clips.send: Jingyang Ridge. Today: Yanggu County, Shandong. A low ridge in western Shandong where, in the novel, Wu Song kills a tiger with his bare hands after 18 bowls of wine. Today it is a park with a tiger statue.

clips.send: Maastricht. The treaty signed here created the European Union and planned a shared currency, the euro.
clips.text: Maastricht. The treaty signed here created the European Union and planned a shared currency, the euro.

clips.send: Great Plains. A huge flat grassland east of the Rocky Mountains. Today it is one of the world’s biggest wheat and corn regions.
clips.text: Great Plains. A huge flat grassland east of the Rocky Mountains. Today it is one of the world’s biggest wheat and corn regions.

clips.send: Strait of Magellan. A twisting, stormy channel between South America and Tierra del Fuego. Magellan’s ships needed 38 days to get through to the Pacific.
clips.text: Strait of Magellan. A twisting, stormy channel between South America and Tierra del Fuego. Magellan’s ships needed 38 days to get through to the Pacific.

clips.send: Maldives. About 1,200 tiny coral islands in the Indian Ocean. Most land is less than 1.5 m above the sea, so rising seas are a real danger.
clips.text: Maldives. About 1,200 tiny coral islands in the Indian Ocean. Most land is less than 1.5 m above the sea, so rising seas are a real danger.

clips.send: Gaocheng Observatory, Dengfeng. Today: Dengfeng, Henan. A brick tower used to measure the sun’s shadow. Guo Shoujing’s calendar fixed the year at 365.2425 days.
clips.text: Gaocheng Observatory, Dengfeng. Today: Dengfeng, Henan. A brick tower used to measure the sun’s shadow. Guo Shoujing’s calendar fixed the year at 365.2425 days.

clips.send: Bay of Bengal. The world’s largest bay, east of India. The Ganges and Brahmaputra pour into it, and strong cyclones often form here.
clips.text: Bay of Bengal. The world’s largest bay, east of India. The Ganges and Brahmaputra pour into it, and strong cyclones often form here.

clips.send: Richmond. Henry Kaiser’s four shipyards in Richmond, California, built 747 ships for World War II — one Liberty ship was put together in under five days. Thousands of women “Rosies” and Black workers from the South worked here; today it is the Rosie the Riveter/WWII Home Front National Historical Park.

clips.send: Tongzhou. Today: Tongzhou District, Beijing. Grain boats from the south unloaded here at the northern end of the canal. Today Tongzhou is Beijing’s new sub-centre for city government offices.

clips.send: Suwannee River. The Suwannee begins in the Okefenokee Swamp and winds about 240 miles south through Florida to the Gulf of Mexico. Tannins from swamp plants stain its water the color of tea, and it is the river in Florida’s state song, “Old Folks at Home.”

clips.send: Kai Tak. Its runway stuck out into Kowloon Bay, and planes flew very low over apartment roofs to land.
clips.text: Kai Tak. Its runway stuck out into Kowloon Bay, and planes flew very low over apartment roofs to land.

clips.send: Oregon City. The end of the Oregon Trail, beside the falls of the Willamette River. In 1844 it became the first incorporated US city west of the Rocky Mountains.
clips.text: Oregon City. The end of the Oregon Trail, beside the falls of the Willamette River. In 1844 it became the first incorporated US city west of the Rocky Mountains.

clips.send: Allegheny Mountains. A long, rugged part of the Appalachians running through Pennsylvania, Maryland and West Virginia. To get trains over them, the Pennsylvania Railroad dug tunnels and built the famous Horseshoe Curve.
clips.text: Allegheny Mountains. A long, rugged part of the Appalachians running through Pennsylvania, Maryland and West Virginia. To get trains over them, the Pennsylvania Railroad dug tunnels and built the famous Horseshoe Curve.

clips.send: Mancheng Han tombs. Today: Mancheng, Baoding, Hebei. The tombs were cut deep into a hillside. Two suits made of jade pieces sewn with gold wire were found inside.
clips.text: Mancheng Han tombs. Today: Mancheng, Baoding, Hebei. The tombs were cut deep into a hillside. Two suits made of jade pieces sewn with gold wire were found inside.

clips.send: Xiao and Xiang Rivers. Today: where the Xiao meets the Xiang, Yongzhou, Hunan. The Xiao River joins the Xiang at Yongzhou; the Xiang then flows north into Dongting Lake. In poems 潇湘 means the lands of southern Hunan — “南极潇湘”.

clips.send: Rabun County. Cherokee mountain land given up in 1817–1819 became Rabun County, in Georgia’s far northeast corner. Its mountains, lakes and the deep Tallulah Gorge on its southern edge make it a favorite place for hikers.

clips.send: Reykjavík. Capital of Iceland, the northernmost capital of a country, at about 64°N. It uses UTC all year round.
clips.text: Reykjavík. Capital of Iceland, the northernmost capital of a country, at about 64°N. It uses UTC all year round.

clips.send: Victoria Harbour. One of the world’s great deep harbours. Over the years much of its edge was filled in to make land.
clips.text: Victoria Harbour. One of the world’s great deep harbours. Over the years much of its edge was filled in to make land.

clips.send: Carter Center. Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter started the Carter Center to watch over fair elections and fight diseases around the world. Its work has nearly wiped out Guinea worm disease — from about 3.5 million cases a year in 1986 to only a handful today; the presidential library and museum share the same hilltop.

clips.send: Mactan. The local chief Lapulapu refused to obey Magellan, and Magellan was killed in the fight. Filipinos remember Lapulapu as a hero.
clips.text: Mactan. The local chief Lapulapu refused to obey Magellan, and Magellan was killed in the fight. Filipinos remember Lapulapu as a hero.

clips.send: Ganges–Brahmaputra Delta. The largest delta on Earth, mostly in Bangladesh. Its Sundarbans mangrove forest is home to Bengal tigers.
clips.text: Ganges–Brahmaputra Delta. The largest delta on Earth, mostly in Bangladesh. Its Sundarbans mangrove forest is home to Bengal tigers.

clips.send: Abilene. In 1867 a businessman built cattle pens next to the Kansas Pacific railroad in this Kansas town, and Texas cowboys drove huge herds up the Chisholm Trail to load them onto trains heading east. Later it was the hometown of President Dwight D. Eisenhower.
clips.text: Abilene. In 1867 a businessman built cattle pens next to the Kansas Pacific railroad in this Kansas town, and Texas cowboys drove huge herds up the Chisholm Trail to load them onto trains heading east. Later it was the hometown of President Dwight D. Eisenhower.

clips.send: Indus Valley. Today: mainly Pakistan. About 4,500 years ago cities here, such as Mohenjo-daro, had brick houses on neat street grids and covered drains.
clips.text: Indus Valley. Today: mainly Pakistan. About 4,500 years ago cities here, such as Mohenjo-daro, had brick houses on neat street grids and covered drains.

clips.send: Ocmulgee Mounds. People have lived here for more than 12,000 years — a Clovis spear point was found here — and around AD 900 Mississippian farmers built a town with big earth mounds. You can climb the 55-foot Great Temple Mound and step inside the Earth Lodge, whose clay floor is about 1,000 years old.

clips.send: Nantong. Nantong lies on the north bank of the Yangtze near its mouth, just across from Shanghai.
clips.text: Nantong. Nantong lies on the north bank of the Yangtze near its mouth, just across from Shanghai.

clips.send: Anchorage. Alaska’s biggest city. In June the Sun shines for over 19 hours a day; in December for less than 6.
clips.text: Anchorage. Alaska’s biggest city. In June the Sun shines for over 19 hours a day; in December for less than 6.

clips.send: Golconda. Late in 1838, Trail of Tears groups crossed the Ohio River into Illinois by ferry at this little river town. The ferry owner charged the Cherokee a dollar a person — about eight times the usual fare.
clips.text: Golconda. Late in 1838, Trail of Tears groups crossed the Ohio River into Illinois by ferry at this little river town. The ferry owner charged the Cherokee a dollar a person — about eight times the usual fare.

clips.send: Lunnan. Today: Luntai County, Xinjiang. An oil and gas field in the Tarim Basin. Gas from here travels about 4,000 km by pipeline to Shanghai.
clips.text: Lunnan. Today: Luntai County, Xinjiang. An oil and gas field in the Tarim Basin. Gas from here travels about 4,000 km by pipeline to Shanghai.

clips.send: Lookout Mountain. A long, flat-topped mountain of the Appalachian Plateau that runs from Georgia into Alabama and Tennessee; Cloudland Canyon is cut into its side. In 1863 Union soldiers won the “Battle Above the Clouds” on its northern end.
clips.text: Lookout Mountain. A long, flat-topped mountain of the Appalachian Plateau that runs from Georgia into Alabama and Tennessee; Cloudland Canyon is cut into its side. In 1863 Union soldiers won the “Battle Above the Clouds” on its northern end.

clips.send: Jinshanling. Today: Luanping, Hebei. Walls and watchtowers ride up and down the mountains. This stretch was built when the general Qi Jiguang guarded the north.
clips.text: Jinshanling. Today: Luanping, Hebei. Walls and watchtowers ride up and down the mountains. This stretch was built when the general Qi Jiguang guarded the north.

clips.send: Titusville. In 1859 Edwin Drake drilled America’s first commercial oil well near this Pennsylvania town, striking oil at 69½ feet. Within a few years the valley was crowded with wooden derricks in a real oil rush.
clips.text: Titusville. In 1859 Edwin Drake drilled America’s first commercial oil well near this Pennsylvania town, striking oil at 69½ feet. Within a few years the valley was crowded with wooden derricks in a real oil rush.

clips.send: Ravenna. The last Western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was removed here in 476. Its churches glitter with Byzantine mosaics of Emperor Justinian.
clips.text: Ravenna. The last Western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was removed here in 476. Its churches glitter with Byzantine mosaics of Emperor Justinian.

clips.send: Alishan. Famous for sunrise over a sea of clouds, giant old cypress trees and a little forest railway that climbs from Chiayi.
clips.text: Alishan. Famous for sunrise over a sea of clouds, giant old cypress trees and a little forest railway that climbs from Chiayi.

clips.send: Qilian Mountains. Snowmelt from the Qilian Mountains feeds the oases of the Hexi Corridor just to the north.
clips.text: Qilian Mountains. Snowmelt from the Qilian Mountains feeds the oases of the Hexi Corridor just to the north.

clips.send: Chishui River. Mao Zedong led the Red Army back and forth across this river four times to confuse and escape the much larger enemy forces.
clips.text: Chishui River. Mao Zedong led the Red Army back and forth across this river four times to confuse and escape the much larger enemy forces.

clips.send: Strait of Hormuz. The narrow sea passage (about 40 km wide at its narrowest) out of the Persian Gulf. About a fifth of the world’s oil passes through it on tankers.
clips.text: Strait of Hormuz. The narrow sea passage (about 40 km wide at its narrowest) out of the Persian Gulf. About a fifth of the world’s oil passes through it on tankers.

clips.send: Lake Pontchartrain Causeway. Today: Louisiana, USA. A pair of low bridges about 38 km long across a lake near New Orleans — one of the longest bridges over water in the world.
clips.text: Lake Pontchartrain Causeway. Today: Louisiana, USA. A pair of low bridges about 38 km long across a lake near New Orleans — one of the longest bridges over water in the world.

clips.send: Tahlequah. After the Trail of Tears the Cherokee made Tahlequah their new capital in 1839, and the last groups arrived in March. The brick Cherokee National Capitol was finished in 1869, and the town’s street signs are written in both English and Cherokee.

clips.text: Junggar Basin. North of the Tian Shan; it holds the Gurbantünggüt Desert and the Karamay oilfield.

clips.send: Mount Hood. Oregon’s highest peak (11,249 feet) is a snow-capped volcano. The Barlow Road, opened in 1846, went around its south side on the last stretch to Oregon City.
clips.text: Mount Hood. Oregon’s highest peak (11,249 feet) is a snow-capped volcano. The Barlow Road, opened in 1846, went around its south side on the last stretch to Oregon City.

clips.send: Mombasa. Goods for much of East Africa arrive here. A new Chinese-built railway, opened in 2017, links the port to Nairobi.
clips.text: Mombasa. Goods for much of East Africa arrive here. A new Chinese-built railway, opened in 2017, links the port to Nairobi.

clips.send: Lothal. A small port town with a big brick basin that many archaeologists think was a dock for ships. Beads and cotton went from here as far as Mesopotamia.
clips.text: Lothal. A small port town with a big brick basin that many archaeologists think was a dock for ships. Beads and cotton went from here as far as Mesopotamia.

clips.send: Greater Khingan Range. A long forested range in the far northeast — one of China’s biggest timber areas. West of it lies the Inner Mongolia Plateau, east of it the Northeast Plain.

clips.send: St. Augustine. Founded 42 years before Jamestown, it is the oldest city in the US that Europeans started and people have lived in ever since. Its fort, the Castillo de San Marcos, is built of coquina, a stone made of tiny shells that swallowed cannonballs instead of cracking.

clips.send: Jianye. Today: Nanjing, Jiangsu. Sun Quan made Jianye the capital of Wu. Later the same city, renamed Jiankang, was the capital of the Eastern Jin and the Southern Dynasties.

clips.send: Tyler Perry Studios. Filmmaker Tyler Perry turned about 330 acres of the old Fort McPherson army base into a studio campus, opened in 2019 — one of the first major studios in the US owned by an African American. It has sound stages named after Black actors and even a full-size copy of the White House.

clips.send: Peachtree Creek. Two days after taking command, Confederate General John Bell Hood attacked Sherman’s army as it crossed this creek just north of Atlanta, but the attack failed. Today the battlefield lies under the Buckhead and Midtown neighborhoods.

Sit-ins spread to dozens of cities, and in July 1960 the counter began serving Black customers; the old store is now the International Civil Rights Center and Museum.

clips.text: Hohhot. Its name means “Blue City” in Mongolian.

clips.send: William Frantz Elementary School. clips.send: Promontory Summit. Today: Golden Spike National Historical Park, Utah. Today working copies of the two locomotives, Jupiter and No. 119, steam up and face each other nose to nose.

clips.send: Appomattox Court House. Today: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park, Virginia. In the parlor of Wilmer McLean’s brick house in this little village, Lee surrendered his army to Grant, and the Civil War was nearly over. Grant let the hungry Confederate soldiers keep their horses and sent them food. Odd fact: McLean had moved here to get away from the war — his old farm was at Bull Run!

In 1846 a treaty split it along the 49th parallel — still the US–Canada border.

clips.send: Little Rock. In September 1957 nine Black students — the Little Rock Nine — tried to enter all-white Central High School in Arkansas’s capital; President Eisenhower sent soldiers of the 101st Airborne to escort them past angry crowds. The school is still open today, and it is also a National Park Service historic site.

Coweta was a “red” town that led in war, while nearby Cusseta was a “white” town for peace.

clips.send: New Orleans. Whoever held this port near the mouth of the Mississippi controlled the river trade, so Jefferson tried to buy it — and in 1803 Napoleon offered all of Louisiana instead. It was the South’s biggest city (and largest slave market) when the US Navy captured it in 1862; in 1960 six-year-old Ruby Bridges integrated a school here.

After the Mexican–American War, Mexico gave up about half its land in the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, and the US paid $15 million. Tens of thousands of Mexicans and many Native nations living there suddenly found themselves inside the United States.

clips.send: Ebenezer. Today: Town site in Effingham County, Georgia. Protestant refugees from Salzburg built this town up the Savannah River. They raised silkworms and spoke out against slavery; the town is gone, but their brick Jerusalem Lutheran Church (1767) still holds services.

clips.send: Pittsburgh. Coal, iron and three rivers made Pittsburgh America’s “Steel City”. Andrew Carnegie’s Edgar Thomson Steel Works opened nearby in 1875 using the Bessemer process, and immigrants from Europe worked its fiery furnaces — it still makes steel today. In 1920 the city’s KDKA began the first regular radio broadcasts.

clips.send: Menlo Park. Today: Edison, New Jersey. Henry Ford later moved the lab building to his museum in Michigan, and the town was renamed Edison.

clips.text: Hongze Lake. Today: Jiangsu. One of China’s five largest freshwater lakes. The eastern route of the South–North Water Diversion pumps water through it on the way north.

clips.send: Port of Brunswick. Georgia’s second deep-water port, one of the busiest US ports for shipping cars and trucks on “roll-on/roll-off” ships.
clips.text: Port of Brunswick. Georgia’s second deep-water port, one of the busiest US ports for shipping cars and trucks on “roll-on/roll-off” ships.

clips.send: Luding Bridge. Today: Luding, Sichuan. An iron-chain bridge built in 1706. The enemy had removed the planks; 22 soldiers climbed across the bare chains under fire and captured it.
clips.text: Luding Bridge. Today: Luding, Sichuan. An iron-chain bridge built in 1706. The enemy had removed the planks; 22 soldiers climbed across the bare chains under fire and captured it.

clips.send: Indian Territory. Today: Oklahoma. The Indian Removal Act of 1830 sent the Cherokee, Creek, Choctaw, Chickasaw and Seminole nations west to this land beyond Arkansas. At the end of the Trail of Tears the Cherokee rebuilt their nation here, with Tahlequah as capital; in 1907 it became part of the state of Oklahoma.

clips.send: Shangjing (Liao capital). Today: Bairin Left Banner, Inner Mongolia. Yelü Abaoji of the Khitan founded the Liao and built this capital on the grasslands.
clips.text: Shangjing (Liao capital). Today: Bairin Left Banner, Inner Mongolia. Yelü Abaoji of the Khitan founded the Liao and built this capital on the grasslands.

clips.send: Singapore. A city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula, on the busy Strait of Malacca.
clips.text: Singapore. A city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula, on the busy Strait of Malacca.

clips.send: Hastings. William of Normandy defeated King Harold here and became king of England. The town that grew on the battlefield is simply called “Battle”.
clips.text: Hastings. William of Normandy defeated King Harold here and became king of England. The town that grew on the battlefield is simply called “Battle”.

clips.send: Vatican and Sistine Chapel. The pope’s own chapel. Michelangelo spent four years painting its ceiling, much of it standing on scaffolding with his head tipped back.
clips.text: Vatican & Sistine Chapel. The pope’s own chapel. Michelangelo spent four years painting its ceiling, much of it standing on scaffolding with his head tipped back.

clips.send: Oregon Trail ruts near Guernsey. Today: Oregon Trail Ruts State Historic Site, Wyoming. So many wagons rolled over this soft sandstone ridge that their wheels wore ruts up to about 5 feet deep. They are some of the best-preserved Oregon Trail ruts anywhere.
clips.text: Oregon Trail ruts near Guernsey. Today: Oregon Trail Ruts State Historic Site, Wyoming. So many wagons rolled over this soft sandstone ridge that their wheels wore ruts up to about 5 feet deep. They are some of the best-preserved Oregon Trail ruts anywhere.

clips.send: Pennsylvania. William Penn, a Quaker, founded it in 1681 as a “holy experiment” where people of every faith could worship freely. Both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution were written in its city of Philadelphia, and in 1863 Lee’s second invasion of the North failed at Gettysburg.

clips.send: Vulture Peak. Today: near Rajgir, Bihar, India. In the novel Lingshan is Buddha’s magic mountain. It is based on a real hill in India where the Buddha preached; the real Xuanzang studied at Nalanda nearby.

clips.send: National Center for Civil and Human Rights. This Atlanta museum next to Centennial Olympic Park tells the story of the civil rights movement and of human rights around the world. At its lunch-counter exhibit you sit on a stool, put on headphones and hear what sit-in protesters faced.

clips.send: Oak Ridge. A whole city built in secret in the Tennessee hills for the Manhattan Project — by 1945 about 75,000 people lived there, yet it was on no map. Its giant plants, running on TVA electricity, made uranium fuel for the atomic bomb.
clips.text: Oak Ridge. A whole city built in secret in the Tennessee hills for the Manhattan Project — by 1945 about 75,000 people lived there, yet it was on no map. Its giant plants, running on TVA electricity, made uranium fuel for the atomic bomb.

clips.send: Ordos Basin. Today: Shaanxi, Gansu, Ningxia and Inner Mongolia. A huge basin rich in coal, oil and natural gas, south of the Yellow River’s great bend.
clips.text: Ordos Basin. Today: Shaanxi, Gansu, Ningxia and Inner Mongolia. A huge basin rich in coal, oil and natural gas, south of the Yellow River’s great bend.

clips.send: Coosa River. The Coosa begins in downtown Rome, where the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers meet, and flows west into Alabama. Riverboats once carried cotton on it.
clips.text: Coosa River. The Coosa begins in downtown Rome, where the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers meet, and flows west into Alabama. Riverboats once carried cotton on it.

clips.send: Silicon Valley. The south end of San Francisco Bay, named for the silicon in computer chips. Intel’s first microprocessor (1971), Apple (1976), Google (1998) and the iPhone (2007) all came from here — and both Apple and Google started in a garage!

clips.send: Port of Los Angeles. Together with its neighbour Long Beach, it handles a big share of the containers coming into the USA, many of them from China.
clips.text: Port of Los Angeles. Together with its neighbour Long Beach, it handles a big share of the containers coming into the USA, many of them from China.

clips.send: Washington, D.C. The nation’s capital, home of Congress, the President and the Supreme Court — the original Declaration of Independence and Constitution are kept at the National Archives here. On August 28, 1963, about 250,000 people filled the National Mall for the March on Washington.

clips.send: Oslo. The capital of Norway, where the Nobel Peace Prize is given every December. In 1964 Martin Luther King Jr. received it here; at 35 he was then the youngest person ever to win it, and he gave all the prize money to the civil rights movement.

clips.send: Stone Forest. Today: Shilin County, Yunnan. Rain slowly dissolved the limestone and left a “forest” of stone pillars, some over 30 m tall.
clips.text: Stone Forest. Today: Shilin County, Yunnan. Rain slowly dissolved the limestone and left a “forest” of stone pillars, some over 30 m tall.

clips.send: Elberton. Elberton calls itself the “Granite Capital of the World”: dozens of quarries and workshops around town cut Piedmont granite into monuments and gravestones. Even its courthouse is trimmed with local granite.
clips.text: Elberton. Elberton calls itself the “Granite Capital of the World”: dozens of quarries and workshops around town cut Piedmont granite into monuments and gravestones. Even its courthouse is trimmed with local granite.

clips.send: Golden Gate Bridge. Today: San Francisco, USA. San Francisco’s famous red suspension bridge, 2.7 km long — a good yardstick for how long China’s new bridges are.
clips.text: Golden Gate Bridge. Today: San Francisco, USA. San Francisco’s famous red suspension bridge, 2.7 km long — a good yardstick for how long China’s new bridges are.

clips.send: Uluru (Ayers Rock). A giant sandstone rock, 348 m high, in the dry Red Centre of Australia. It is sacred to the Anangu people and glows red at sunset.
clips.text: Uluru (Ayers Rock). A giant sandstone rock, 348 m high, in the dry Red Centre of Australia. It is sacred to the Anangu people and glows red at sunset.

clips.send: Ceylon. Today: Sri Lanka. A stone tablet Zheng He set up at Galle in 1409 is written in Chinese, Tamil and Persian. It is now in the Colombo National Museum.
clips.text: Ceylon. Today: Sri Lanka. A stone tablet Zheng He set up at Galle in 1409 is written in Chinese, Tamil and Persian. It is now in the Colombo National Museum.

clips.send: Auschwitz-Birkenau. Today: Oświęcim, Poland. The largest Nazi camp, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered. It is now a memorial so that the world remembers.
clips.text: Auschwitz-Birkenau. Today: Oświęcim, Poland. The largest Nazi camp, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered. It is now a memorial so that the world remembers.

clips.send: Fenghuoshan Tunnel. Today: Qinghai, on the Qinghai–Tibet Railway. The highest railway tunnel in the world on permafrost — engineers kept the frozen ground cold so the tunnel would not sink.
clips.text: Fenghuoshan Tunnel. Today: Qinghai, on the Qinghai–Tibet Railway. The highest railway tunnel in the world on permafrost — engineers kept the frozen ground cold so the tunnel would not sink.

clips.send: Dadu. Today: Beijing. Kublai Khan built Dadu on a neat grid plan. Parts of its earth wall survive as a park in northern Beijing.
clips.text: Dadu. Today: Beijing. Kublai Khan built Dadu on a neat grid plan. Parts of its earth wall survive as a park in northern Beijing.

clips.send: Sinai Peninsula. A rocky, dry triangle of land that joins Africa to Asia. Egyptians came here for copper and turquoise, not to farm.
clips.text: Sinai Peninsula. A rocky, dry triangle of land that joins Africa to Asia. Egyptians came here for copper and turquoise, not to farm.

clips.send: Lianyungang. A port in northern Jiangsu; trains from here cross Asia to Europe. Its Huaguo Mountain is linked with the Monkey King story.
clips.text: Lianyungang. A port in northern Jiangsu; trains from here cross Asia to Europe. Its Huaguo Mountain is linked with the Monkey King story.

clips.send: Auburn Avenue. When segregation kept Black Atlantans out of white businesses, they built their own here — banks, insurance companies, newspapers and churches — and “Sweet Auburn” was called “the richest Black street in the world”. Martin Luther King Jr. was born on this street in 1929.

clips.send: Statue of Liberty. France gave this copper statue to the United States, and it was dedicated in 1886; Emma Lazarus’s poem on the pedestal welcomes the “huddled masses yearning to breathe free”. It was once copper-brown and slowly turned green — and even with its pedestal it is shorter than a Saturn V rocket.

clips.send: San Antonio. Founded by the Spanish in 1718 around a chain of missions, one of which was the Alamo, besieged in 1836. Today the River Walk winds through downtown below street level, lined with cafés.
clips.text: San Antonio. Founded by the Spanish in 1718 around a chain of missions, one of which was the Alamo, besieged in 1836. Today the River Walk winds through downtown below street level, lined with cafés.

clips.send: Himalayas. An arc of snowy peaks on China’s southwest border, including Mount Qomolangma (Everest).
clips.text: Himalayas. An arc of snowy peaks on China’s southwest border, including Mount Qomolangma (Everest).

clips.send: Miami. A big city near the southern tip of Florida, only about 230 miles from Havana. During the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis it was well within range of the Soviet missiles in Cuba.
clips.text: Miami. A big city near the southern tip of Florida, only about 230 miles from Havana. During the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis it was well within range of the Soviet missiles in Cuba.

clips.send: Old Governor’s Mansion. Finished in 1839 in grand Greek Revival style, it was home to Georgia’s governors while Milledgeville was the capital, and General Sherman made it his headquarters in November 1864. Today it is a museum that also tells the stories of the enslaved people who worked there.

clips.text: Colosseum. About 50,000 people could watch gladiator fights here. Its arches and vaults are still copied in stadiums today.

clips.send: Nansha Islands. Hundreds of islands, reefs and banks spread over a huge area of sea.
clips.text: Nansha Islands. Hundreds of islands, reefs and banks spread over a huge area of sea.

clips.send: Yongding River. It used to flood so often that it was called the “river without a fixed course”; the Qing renamed it Yongding, “forever steady”. The Lugou Bridge crosses it.
clips.text: Yongding River. It used to flood so often that it was called the “river without a fixed course”; the Qing renamed it Yongding, “forever steady”. The Lugou Bridge crosses it.

clips.send: Manzanar. Today: Manzanar National Historic Site, California. After Executive Order 9066 in 1942, more than 10,000 Japanese Americans — most of them US citizens — were forced to live behind barbed wire in this dusty camp below the Sierra Nevada. Ansel Adams photographed daily life here with Mt. Williamson rising behind, and a guard tower has been rebuilt at the site.

clips.send: Tarim River. Fed by melting snow from the mountains, it flows along the edge of the Taklamakan and never reaches the sea. Desert poplar forests grow along its banks.

clips.text: International Date Line. A line in the Pacific, mostly along 180° longitude, where the calendar date changes. Cross it going west and you skip ahead one day.

clips.send: Americus. In 1963 police arrested young civil rights protesters here, and four leaders were charged with “insurrection”, a crime that could bring the death penalty, before a federal court freed them. Americus is also where Habitat for Humanity, which builds homes around the world, began in 1976.

He closed the restaurant rather than serve Black customers — and two years later was elected governor.

clips.send: New York. The Dutch town of New Amsterdam became English New York in 1664, and in 1789 the first Congress under the Constitution met here. The Erie Canal made it the nation’s busiest port, millions of immigrants arrived here, and in 1882 Edison’s Pearl Street station began lighting its streets with electricity.

clips.send: Red River (Texas–Oklahoma). Named for its reddish mud, this river forms much of the border between Texas and Oklahoma. In 1819 the US and Spain agreed to make it part of the boundary between their lands.

clips.send: Sunbury. Today: Historic site in Liberty County. Once a busy port that rivaled Savannah. In November 1778 the British demanded the surrender of its Fort Morris, and Col. John McIntosh answered “Come and take it!”; after the war the town faded away, and only its old cemetery is left.

clips.send: Moscow. Its fortress, the Kremlin, and Red Square are at the centre. In 1941 the German army was stopped just outside the city.

clips.send: Darien. Highland Scots founded Darien in 1736 to guard the frontier, and in 1739 they signed a petition against bringing slavery into Georgia. After the Civil War, Tunis Campbell organized freedpeople here and was elected a state senator.

clips.send: Mekong River. It starts on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau in China, where it is called the Lancang, and flows through six countries. Its delta in Vietnam is one of Asia’s great rice bowls.

clips.send: Java. Today: Java, Indonesia. A big island of Indonesia that Zheng He’s fleet visited. Today more than 150 million people live there.
clips.text: Java. Today: Java, Indonesia. A big island of Indonesia that Zheng He’s fleet visited. Today more than 150 million people live there.

clips.send: Great Hall of the People. Today: West side of Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. The National People’s Congress meets here. Its main auditorium seats about 10,000 people.

clips.send: Hadrian’s Wall. A stone wall about 118 km long across northern Britain, guarding the edge of the Roman Empire. Soldiers lived in forts along it.
clips.text: Hadrian’s Wall. A stone wall about 118 km long across northern Britain, guarding the edge of the Roman Empire. Soldiers lived in forts along it.

clips.text: Lübeck. The leading city of the Hanseatic League, a group of trading towns around the North Sea and the Baltic. Its brick city gate, the Holstentor, still stands.

clips.send: Independence, Missouri. In the 1840s wagon trains bought oxen, flour and supplies here before starting the 2,000-mile Oregon Trail. Today the National Frontier Trails Museum tells their story.

clips.text: Mount Danxia. Today: Shaoguan, Guangdong. Red sandstone cliffs that gave their name to the “Danxia” landform found all over China.

clips.send: Shibadong Village. Today: Huayuan County, Xiangxi, Hunan. A Miao village in the mountains of western Hunan. It found its way out of poverty by growing kiwi fruit, opening family guesthouses and selling local crafts.

clips.send: Creek (Muscogee) Nation. Today: Central and western Georgia, eastern Alabama. Treaty by treaty its land was taken: by 1827 no Creek land was left in Georgia, and in 1836 most Creek people were forced west to Indian Territory.

clips.send: Miaodao Islands. Today: Changdao, Yantai, Shandong. About 30 islands strung between Shandong and Liaodong.
clips.text: Miaodao Islands. Today: Changdao, Yantai, Shandong. About 30 islands strung between Shandong and Liaodong.

clips.send: Dunhuang Yardang National Geopark. Today: Northwest of Dunhuang, Gansu. Rows of clay ridges carved by strong desert winds. At night the wind howls through them, so people call it the “Ghost City”.
clips.text: Dunhuang Yardang National Geopark. Today: Northwest of Dunhuang, Gansu. Rows of clay ridges carved by strong desert winds. At night the wind howls through them, so people call it the “Ghost City”.

clips.send: Potala Palace. Today: Lhasa, Tibet. Tradition says Songtsen Gampo first built a palace here for Princess Wencheng. The red-and-white palace climbs the whole hill.
clips.text: Potala Palace. Today: Lhasa, Tibet. Tradition says Songtsen Gampo first built a palace here for Princess Wencheng. The red-and-white palace climbs the whole hill.

clips.send: Albuquerque. Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft in this New Mexico city in 1975, to be near the company that made the Altair computer; in 1979 they moved to Washington State. Every October hundreds of hot-air balloons fill its sky at the Balloon Fiesta.

clips.send: Tallulah River. This mountain river carved Tallulah Gorge, about 2 miles long and nearly 1,000 feet deep. In 1970 the tightrope walker Karl Wallenda crossed the gorge on a wire — doing two headstands along the way!
clips.text: Tallulah River. This mountain river carved Tallulah Gorge, about 2 miles long and nearly 1,000 feet deep. In 1970 the tightrope walker Karl Wallenda crossed the gorge on a wire — doing two headstands along the way!

clips.send: South China. Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan and nearby: the warmest, rainiest part of mainland China. The rainy season starts here in May.
clips.text: South China. Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan and nearby: the warmest, rainiest part of mainland China. The rainy season starts here in May.

clips.send: Jiajin Mountain. Over 4,000 m high with thin air and snow. Many soldiers in thin clothes froze on the way up.
clips.text: Jiajin Mountain. Over 4,000 m high with thin air and snow. Many soldiers in thin clothes froze on the way up.

clips.send: Zhongsha Islands. Most of the Zhongsha group is hidden under the sea; only rocks of Huangyan Island stick out.
clips.text: Zhongsha Islands. Most of the Zhongsha group is hidden under the sea; only rocks of Huangyan Island stick out.

clips.send: Drum Tower and Bell Tower. Drums sounded the hours at night and the bell rang at dawn. The bronze bell in the Bell Tower weighs about 63 tonnes.
clips.text: Drum Tower and Bell Tower. Drums sounded the hours at night and the bell rang at dawn. The bronze bell in the Bell Tower weighs about 63 tonnes.

clips.send: Rotterdam. Europe’s largest seaport, in the Netherlands, where the Rhine reaches the North Sea.
clips.text: Rotterdam. Europe’s largest seaport, in the Netherlands, where the Rhine reaches the North Sea.

clips.send: Frankfurt. Today: Frankfurt am Main, Germany. Many Berlin Airlift flights took off from here. Today the European Central Bank, which looks after the euro, has its tower in Frankfurt.
clips.text: Frankfurt. Today: Frankfurt am Main, Germany. Many Berlin Airlift flights took off from here. Today the European Central Bank, which looks after the euro, has its tower in Frankfurt.

clips.send: Sutter’s Mill. Today: Coloma, California. On 24 January 1848 James Marshall spotted shiny flakes in the ditch below the sawmill he was building for John Sutter — gold! The Gold Rush brought about 300,000 people to California, and for California’s Native peoples it brought disaster.
clips.text: Sutter’s Mill. Today: Coloma, California. On 24 January 1848 James Marshall spotted shiny flakes in the ditch below the sawmill he was building for John Sutter — gold! The Gold Rush brought about 300,000 people to California, and for California’s Native peoples it brought disaster.

clips.send: Dubai. A city of skyscrapers in the United Arab Emirates, built in the desert with money from oil and trade. Its Burj Khalifa (828 m) is the tallest building in the world.
clips.text: Dubai. A city of skyscrapers in the United Arab Emirates, built in the desert with money from oil and trade. Its Burj Khalifa (828 m) is the tallest building in the world.

clips.send: Talas. Today: Taraz area, Kazakhstan. The only big battle between Tang China and the Abbasid Caliphate. The traditional story says captured Chinese papermakers then spread paper-making west.
clips.text: Talas. Today: Taraz area, Kazakhstan. The only big battle between Tang China and the Abbasid Caliphate. The traditional story says captured Chinese papermakers then spread paper-making west.

clips.send: Fort Cass. Today: Charleston, Tennessee. Thousands of Cherokee were held in crowded camps around Fort Cass in the hot summer of 1838, and many died of disease. Chief John Ross won the right for the Cherokee to lead their own removal, and most groups set out from here in the fall.

clips.send: St. Marys River. It flows out of the Okefenokee Swamp and loops around to the Atlantic, forming the border between Georgia and Florida. It became Georgia’s southern border in 1763.
clips.text: St. Marys River. It flows out of the Okefenokee Swamp and loops around to the Atlantic, forming the border between Georgia and Florida. It became Georgia’s southern border in 1763.

clips.send: Charleston, Tennessee. This small town on the Hiwassee River grew up around Fort Cass, the center of the 1838 removal camps. Thousands of Cherokee waited here through a hot, sickly summer before the long walk west.
clips.text: Charleston, Tennessee. This small town on the Hiwassee River grew up around Fort Cass, the center of the 1838 removal camps. Thousands of Cherokee waited here through a hot, sickly summer before the long walk west.

clips.send: Harlem. A neighborhood in northern Manhattan that became the heart of Black culture in the 1920s Harlem Renaissance — poet Langston Hughes, writer Zora Neale Hurston and jazz stars like Duke Ellington and Louis Armstrong. The Apollo Theater still holds its famous Amateur Night.

clips.send: Yaksa. Today: Albazino, Russia. Russian forces built a fort here on the Heilongjiang. Kangxi’s army besieged it twice and won; then the two sides signed the Treaty of Nerchinsk.
clips.text: Yaksa. Today: Albazino, Russia. Russian forces built a fort here on the Heilongjiang. Kangxi’s army besieged it twice and won; then the two sides signed the Treaty of Nerchinsk.

clips.send: Yungang Grottoes. Today: West of Datong, Shanxi. More than 50,000 Buddhist statues are carved into a sandstone cliff near the old Northern Wei capital Pingcheng. The biggest Buddha is about 17 m tall.
clips.text: Yungang Grottoes. Today: West of Datong, Shanxi. More than 50,000 Buddhist statues are carved into a sandstone cliff near the old Northern Wei capital Pingcheng. The biggest Buddha is about 17 m tall.

clips.send: Dhaka. Capital of Bangladesh, on the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta — one of the most crowded cities on Earth.
clips.text: Dhaka. Capital of Bangladesh, on the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta — one of the most crowded cities on Earth.

clips.send: Wusong. Today: Baoshan District, Shanghai. In 1876 a British company opened China’s first railway, a line of about 15 km from Shanghai to Wusong at the mouth of the Huangpu River. The Qing government bought it the next year — and tore it up.
clips.text: Wusong. Today: Baoshan District, Shanghai. In 1876 a British company opened China’s first railway, a line of about 15 km from Shanghai to Wusong at the mouth of the Huangpu River. The Qing government bought it the next year — and tore it up.

clips.send: Frombork. Nicolaus Copernicus worked at the cathedral of this small Baltic town and watched the sky from its walls. He is buried in the cathedral.
clips.text: Frombork. Nicolaus Copernicus worked at the cathedral of this small Baltic town and watched the sky from its walls. He is buried in the cathedral.

clips.send: Lingqu Canal. Today: Xing’an, Guangxi. Linking the north-flowing Xiang River with the south-flowing Li River, it joined the Yangtze and Pearl river systems so Qin ships could reach Lingnan.
clips.text: Lingqu Canal. Today: Xing’an, Guangxi. Linking the north-flowing Xiang River with the south-flowing Li River, it joined the Yangtze and Pearl river systems so Qin ships could reach Lingnan.

clips.send: National Constitution Center. A museum about the Constitution on Independence Mall in Philadelphia, opened in 2003. In Signers’ Hall you can stand among life-size bronze statues of 42 delegates of the 1787 Convention.
clips.text: National Constitution Center. A museum about the Constitution on Independence Mall in Philadelphia, opened in 2003. In Signers’ Hall you can stand among life-size bronze statues of 42 delegates of the 1787 Convention.

clips.send: Wangxia. Today: Macao. In 1844 China and the United States signed their first treaty in this village, the Treaty of Wangxia; it was one of the unequal treaties forced on China after the Opium War. It was signed at the Kun Iam Temple, where a round stone table from that day is still kept.

clips.send: Chesapeake Bay. On 5 September 1781 a French fleet under Admiral de Grasse drove off the British navy at the mouth of this bay, so no ships could rescue Cornwallis at Yorktown. The Chesapeake is the largest estuary in the United States.
clips.text: Chesapeake Bay. On 5 September 1781 a French fleet under Admiral de Grasse drove off the British navy at the mouth of this bay, so no ships could rescue Cornwallis at Yorktown. The Chesapeake is the largest estuary in the United States.

clips.send: Nanchang. The Nanchang Uprising fired the first shot of armed resistance against the Nationalists. 1 August is now the founding day of the People’s Liberation Army.
clips.text: Nanchang. The Nanchang Uprising fired the first shot of armed resistance against the Nationalists. 1 August is now the founding day of the People’s Liberation Army.

clips.send: Bohai Sea. Almost surrounded by Liaoning, Hebei, Tianjin and Shandong. It is shallow — only about 18 m deep on average — and parts freeze in winter.
clips.text: Bohai Sea. Almost surrounded by Liaoning, Hebei, Tianjin and Shandong. It is shallow — only about 18 m deep on average — and parts freeze in winter.

clips.send: Lowell. Water-powered textile mills along the Merrimack River employed thousands of young women, the “mill girls”.
clips.text: Lowell. Water-powered textile mills along the Merrimack River employed thousands of young women, the “mill girls”.

clips.send: Nagasaki. Three days after Hiroshima, a second atomic bomb hit Nagasaki. Its Peace Park calls for a world without nuclear weapons.
clips.text: Nagasaki. Three days after Hiroshima, a second atomic bomb hit Nagasaki. Its Peace Park calls for a world without nuclear weapons.

clips.send: Savannah. Oglethorpe laid Savannah out in 1733 as neighborhoods around shady squares — 22 of those squares are still there. Sherman’s March to the Sea ended here in 1864, and today it has one of the busiest container ports in the country.
clips.text: Savannah. Oglethorpe laid Savannah out in 1733 as neighborhoods around shady squares — 22 of those squares are still there. Sherman’s March to the Sea ended here in 1864, and today it has one of the busiest container ports in the country.

clips.send: Grand Canyon. About 446 km long and up to 1.8 km deep. Its walls show rock layers almost 2 billion years old, like pages in a history book.
clips.text: Grand Canyon. About 446 km long and up to 1.8 km deep. Its walls show rock layers almost 2 billion years old, like pages in a history book.

clips.send: Maryland. Lord Baltimore founded it in 1634 as a refuge for Catholics, and its Toleration Act of 1649 protected Christians of different churches. In the Civil War it was a slave state that stayed in the Union, and Lee’s first invasion of the North was stopped here at Antietam.
clips.text: Maryland. Lord Baltimore founded it in 1634 as a refuge for Catholics, and its Toleration Act of 1649 protected Christians of different churches. In the Civil War it was a slave state that stayed in the Union, and Lee’s first invasion of the North was stopped here at Antietam.

clips.send: Chaozhou. Today: Chaozhou and Shantou, Guangdong. Chaozhou is an old city famous for its Guangji Bridge and its tea culture. The treaty port was set up at Shantou on the coast.
clips.text: Chaozhou. Today: Chaozhou and Shantou, Guangdong. Chaozhou is an old city famous for its Guangji Bridge and its tea culture. The treaty port was set up at Shantou on the coast.

clips.send: Gainesville. The “Poultry Capital of the World”: Gainesville led Georgia’s switch from cotton to raising broiler chickens, and a statue of a chicken stands in its Poultry Park. Lake Lanier lies right next to town.
clips.text: Gainesville. The “Poultry Capital of the World”: Gainesville led Georgia’s switch from cotton to raising broiler chickens, and a statue of a chicken stands in its Poultry Park. Lake Lanier lies right next to town.

clips.send: Castle Garden. Today: Castle Clinton National Monument, Battery Park, New York. Before Ellis Island, about 8 million immigrants entered America through this round stone fort at the tip of Manhattan. Built as a fort before the War of 1812, it later became a concert hall and even an aquarium — today it is Castle Clinton, where you buy ferry tickets to the Statue of Liberty.

clips.send: Marathon. Athenian soldiers beat a much bigger Persian army on this plain. The story of a runner carrying the news 40 km to Athens gave us the marathon race.
clips.text: Marathon. Athenian soldiers beat a much bigger Persian army on this plain. The story of a runner carrying the news 40 km to Athens gave us the marathon race.

clips.send: Kwai Tsing Container Terminals. Giant cranes load ships with containers on land reclaimed from the sea.
clips.text: Kwai Tsing Container Terminals. Giant cranes load ships with containers on land reclaimed from the sea.

clips.send: Louisville. Named for King Louis XVI of France, who had helped America win independence. In 1796 the legislature publicly burned the papers of the corrupt Yazoo land sale here — legend says the fire was lit with a magnifying glass and sunlight.
clips.text: Louisville. Named for King Louis XVI of France, who had helped America win independence. In 1796 the legislature publicly burned the papers of the corrupt Yazoo land sale here — legend says the fire was lit with a magnifying glass and sunlight.

clips.send: Glynn County. Home of Brunswick and most of the Golden Isles on Georgia’s coast. Its old 1907 courthouse sits in a park shaded by huge live oaks draped with Spanish moss.
clips.text: Glynn County. Home of Brunswick and most of the Golden Isles on Georgia’s coast. Its old 1907 courthouse sits in a park shaded by huge live oaks draped with Spanish moss.

clips.send: Sanya. Sanya is about 18° N — but China’s southernmost point, Zengmu Ansha, is much farther south.
clips.text: Sanya. Sanya is about 18° N — but China’s southernmost point, Zengmu Ansha, is much farther south.

clips.send: St. Paul. Minnesota’s capital, on the Mississippi River. From here James J. Hill’s Great Northern Railway reached all the way to Seattle in 1893 — built without the free government land the other transcontinental lines got.
clips.text: St. Paul. Minnesota’s capital, on the Mississippi River. From here James J. Hill’s Great Northern Railway reached all the way to Seattle in 1893 — built without the free government land the other transcontinental lines got.

clips.send: Acropolis and Parthenon. The “high city” is a rocky hill in the middle of Athens. The Parthenon on top was a marble temple for the goddess Athena.
clips.text: Acropolis & Parthenon. The “high city” is a rocky hill in the middle of Athens. The Parthenon on top was a marble temple for the goddess Athena.

clips.send: Juyong Pass. The wall climbs both sides of a narrow valley here to guard the road to the capital. It is one of the most famous passes of the Great Wall.
clips.text: Juyong Pass. The wall climbs both sides of a narrow valley here to guard the road to the capital. It is one of the most famous passes of the Great Wall.

clips.send: Boao. A seaside town in Hainan where the Boao Forum for Asia meets every year to discuss Asia’s development.
clips.text: Boao. A seaside town in Hainan where the Boao Forum for Asia meets every year to discuss Asia’s development.

clips.send: Kitty Hawk. The Wright brothers picked these windy sand dunes on North Carolina’s Outer Banks for steady winds and soft landings. On 17 December 1903 Orville flew 120 feet in 12 seconds — shorter than the wingspan of a jumbo jet. A granite monument now crowns Big Kill Devil Hill.

clips.send: Mitad del Mundo. “The middle of the world”: an equator monument just north of Quito, Ecuador. One foot in each hemisphere!
clips.text: Mitad del Mundo. “The middle of the world”: an equator monument just north of Quito, Ecuador. One foot in each hemisphere!

clips.send: Three Gorges Dam. Today: Sandouping, Yichang, Hubei. The dam is 2,335 m long and 181 m high. It controls floods, makes clean electricity and lets big ships sail to Chongqing.
clips.text: Three Gorges Dam. Today: Sandouping, Yichang, Hubei. The dam is 2,335 m long and 181 m high. It controls floods, makes clean electricity and lets big ships sail to Chongqing.

clips.send: Yunzhong. Today: around Togtoh, Inner Mongolia. The general Wei Shang guarded Yunzhong against the Xiongnu; the emperor sent Feng Tang to pardon him. Su Shi’s “持节云中” hopes the court will call him back the same way.

clips.send: Dallas. A big city in north Texas, one of the cities in the lesson’s missile-range calculator: Soviet missiles in Cuba could have reached it. In 1963 President Kennedy was assassinated here.
clips.text: Dallas. A big city in north Texas, one of the cities in the lesson’s missile-range calculator: Soviet missiles in Cuba could have reached it. In 1963 President Kennedy was assassinated here.

clips.send: Oconee River. It flows from the hills near Athens south past Milledgeville and joins the Ocmulgee to form the Altamaha. After the treaties of 1783 and 1790 it was the border between Georgia’s settlers and the Creek Nation.

clips.send: Mount Langya. Today: southwest of Chuzhou, Anhui. Wooded hills just southwest of Chuzhou — “蔚然而深秀者, 琅琊也”. The Niang Spring and the Old Drunkard’s Pavilion are in its valleys.

clips.send: Fort McAllister. This fort of earth and sand on the Ogeechee River had beaten off Union warships, but on December 13, 1864 Hazen’s soldiers stormed it in about 15 minutes. That opened a link to the Union fleet, and Savannah fell days later.

clips.send: Strait of Malacca. A narrow sea lane between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra — the shortest way between the Pacific and the Indian Ocean. Many big ships still pass it every day.
clips.text: Strait of Malacca. A narrow sea lane between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra — the shortest way between the Pacific and the Indian Ocean. Many big ships still pass it every day.

clips.send: Carthage. Today: near Tunis, Tunisia. A Phoenician trading city whose general Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome. Romans later rebuilt it as a Roman city.
clips.text: Carthage. Today: near Tunis, Tunisia. A Phoenician trading city whose general Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome. Romans later rebuilt it as a Roman city.

clips.send: Arabian Peninsula. The world’s largest peninsula, mostly desert. Around 610 Muhammad began preaching Islam in Mecca here.
clips.text: Arabian Peninsula. The world’s largest peninsula, mostly desert. Around 610 Muhammad began preaching Islam in Mecca here.

clips.send: Yichang. The river leaves the gorges and spreads out onto the plain here — the “gateway to the Three Gorges”.
clips.text: Yichang. The river leaves the gorges and spreads out onto the plain here — the “gateway to the Three Gorges”.

clips.send: Thomas Edison National Historical Park. In 1887 Edison moved to a much bigger laboratory in West Orange, New Jersey, where his team built movie cameras and better phonographs. Visitors can see his lab, his huge library and a copy of the “Black Maria”, the first movie studio.
clips.text: Thomas Edison National Historical Park. In 1887 Edison moved to a much bigger laboratory in West Orange, New Jersey, where his team built movie cameras and better phonographs. Visitors can see his lab, his huge library and a copy of the “Black Maria”, the first movie studio.

clips.send: New England. Rocky soil and long winters made farming hard, so New Englanders fished, cut timber and built ships; most towns were founded by Puritans who wanted to worship in their own way. From 1872, 120 Chinese boys came here to study.
clips.text: New England. Rocky soil and long winters made farming hard, so New Englanders fished, cut timber and built ships; most towns were founded by Puritans who wanted to worship in their own way. From 1872, 120 Chinese boys came here to study.

clips.send: Pompeii. When Vesuvius erupted, ash buried the whole town. Digging it out shows us Roman streets, shops, bakeries and paintings just as they were.
clips.text: Pompeii. When Vesuvius erupted, ash buried the whole town. Digging it out shows us Roman streets, shops, bakeries and paintings just as they were.

clips.send: Salado. A small Texas town on the old Chisholm Trail between Waco and Austin. Cowboys driving cattle north to Kansas passed through, and the Stagecoach Inn still welcomes travelers today.
clips.text: Salado. A small Texas town on the old Chisholm Trail between Waco and Austin. Cowboys driving cattle north to Kansas passed through, and the Stagecoach Inn still welcomes travelers today.

clips.send: Mizhou. Today: Zhucheng, Shandong. Here Su Shi led the hunt of 《江城子·密州出猎》 (1075) and, on the Chaoran Terrace he rebuilt, wrote 《水调歌头》 for his brother at Mid-Autumn 1076.

clips.text: Changsha. A lively city on the Xiang River. Orange Isle in the river and the Han tombs at Mawangdui are famous.

clips.send: Missouri. Missouri joined the Union as a slave state in the Missouri Compromise of 1820, and its towns were the starting points of the Oregon and Santa Fe trails. In the winter of 1839 Trail of Tears groups crossed it, and in the Civil War it was a border slave state that stayed in the Union.

clips.send: Sea of Japan. The sea between the Korean Peninsula, Russia and the islands of Japan.
clips.text: Sea of Japan. The sea between the Korean Peninsula, Russia and the islands of Japan.

clips.send: Yutian (Khotan). Today: Hotan, Xinjiang. Famous for its white jade, carried east to the Central Plains for thousands of years.
clips.text: Yutian (Khotan). Today: Hotan, Xinjiang. Famous for its white jade, carried east to the Central Plains for thousands of years.

clips.send: Inner Mongolia. A long region across northern China with wide grasslands — China’s largest pastoral area, famous for Sanhe horses and cattle.
clips.text: Inner Mongolia. A long region across northern China with wide grasslands — China’s largest pastoral area, famous for Sanhe horses and cattle.

clips.send: Jianghuai region. The land between the Yangtze and the Huai rivers, in Anhui and Jiangsu — rice and wheat both grow here.
clips.text: Jianghuai region. The land between the Yangtze and the Huai rivers, in Anhui and Jiangsu — rice and wheat both grow here.

clips.send: Vidalia. This small Coastal Plain town gave its name to Vidalia onions, so sweet that some people bite into them like apples. By law, only onions grown in about 20 counties around Vidalia may carry the name.
clips.text: Vidalia. This small Coastal Plain town gave its name to Vidalia onions, so sweet that some people bite into them like apples. By law, only onions grown in about 20 counties around Vidalia may carry the name.

clips.send: Datong–Qinhuangdao Railway. A railway built just for coal, from Datong in Shanxi to the port of Qinhuangdao. Its heavy trains carry hundreds of millions of tonnes a year.
clips.text: Datong–Qinhuangdao Railway. A railway built just for coal, from Datong in Shanxi to the port of Qinhuangdao. Its heavy trains carry hundreds of millions of tonnes a year.

clips.send: Shennong Stream. Today: Badong, Hubei. Boatmen used to pull small boats called “pea-pod boats” up its rapids by rope.
clips.text: Shennong Stream. Today: Badong, Hubei. Boatmen used to pull small boats called “pea-pod boats” up its rapids by rope.

clips.send: Trent. Today: Trento, Italy. Catholic bishops met here on and off for 18 years to answer the Protestants and reform their own Church.
clips.text: Trent. Today: Trento, Italy. Catholic bishops met here on and off for 18 years to answer the Protestants and reform their own Church.

clips.send: The Harmas (Fabre’s garden). Today: Sérignan-du-Comtat, France. A stony, weedy garden in Provence that Jean-Henri Fabre bought so he could watch insects at home. He wrote most of The Insect World (《昆虫记》) here.

clips.send: Russell–Brasstown Scenic Byway. A 41-mile scenic loop road through the Chattahoochee National Forest in the Blue Ridge Mountains. It passes the road up to Brasstown Bald, Georgia’s highest point, and is especially colorful in fall.

clips.text: Jiujiang. A river port on the Yangtze at the foot of Mount Lu, near Poyang Lake. It became a busy market for tea, rice and porcelain.

clips.send: UCLA. On 29 October 1969 a student in Leonard Kleinrock’s lab tried to type “LOGIN” to a computer at SRI — the system crashed after “LO”, so the first message on ARPANET, the internet’s ancestor, was “LO”. The room, 3420 Boelter Hall, is now a small museum.

clips.send: New Netherland. Today: New York and New Jersey. The Dutch built fur-trading posts along the Hudson River and the town of New Amsterdam on Manhattan. In 1664 English warships sailed in, the Dutch gave up without a fight, and New Amsterdam became New York.

clips.send: Hoover Dam. Thousands of workers desperate for Depression-era jobs built this 726-foot concrete dam across the Colorado River, between Nevada and Arizona; it was begun under President Hoover and finished in 1936 under FDR. It holds back Lake Mead and makes electricity for millions of people.

clips.send: Tuskegee Institute. Today: Tuskegee University, Alabama. Booker T. Washington led this school for Black students, and from 1896 George Washington Carver taught farmers here to rotate crops like peanuts and sweet potatoes. From 1941 the Tuskegee Airmen, the first Black military pilots, learned to fly at nearby Moton Field, where the old hangars are now a national historic site.

clips.send: Shanksville. On 11 September 2001 the passengers and crew of United Flight 93 fought back against the hijackers, and the plane crashed in a field near this Pennsylvania village instead of reaching Washington. The memorial’s Tower of Voices holds 40 wind chimes, one for each person on board.

clips.text: Dublin. A Coastal Plain city on the Oconee River, only about 220 feet above sea level. Named after Dublin, Ireland, it throws a big St. Patrick’s Day festival every March.

clips.send: Junshan Island. Today: Dongting Lake, Yueyang, Hunan. A small island in Dongting Lake opposite Yueyang Tower — the “distant mountain” the lake holds in its mouth. Liu Yuxi compared it to a green snail on a silver plate.
clips.text: Junshan Island. Today: Dongting Lake, Yueyang, Hunan. A small island in Dongting Lake opposite Yueyang Tower — the “distant mountain” the lake holds in its mouth. Liu Yuxi compared it to a green snail on a silver plate.

clips.send: Tordesillas. Spain and Portugal drew a line down the Atlantic here and split the newly reached lands between them — without asking anyone who lived there.
clips.text: Tordesillas. Spain and Portugal drew a line down the Atlantic here and split the newly reached lands between them — without asking anyone who lived there.

clips.send: Kraków. The old capital of Poland, with one of Europe’s biggest medieval market squares. Young Copernicus studied at its university.
clips.text: Kraków. The old capital of Poland, with one of Europe’s biggest medieval market squares. Young Copernicus studied at its university.

clips.send: Greenland. The world’s largest island (about 2.2 million square kilometers ), mostly buried under an ice sheet up to 3 km thick. Only about 57,000 people live there, on the coast.
clips.text: Greenland. The world’s largest island (about 2.2 million km²), mostly buried under an ice sheet up to 3 km thick. Only about 57,000 people live there, on the coast.

clips.send: Cape Canaveral. Explorer 1, Alan Shepard, John Glenn and Apollo 11 all lifted off from this stretch of the Florida coast. Moon rockets were stacked in the Vehicle Assembly Building, whose doors — 456 feet high — are the tallest in the world.
clips.text: Cape Canaveral. Explorer 1, Alan Shepard, John Glenn and Apollo 11 all lifted off from this stretch of the Florida coast. Moon rockets were stacked in the Vehicle Assembly Building, whose doors — 456 feet high — are the tallest in the world.

clips.send: Liuyang. Liuyang has made fireworks for many centuries and is called the “home of fireworks” — one of gunpowder’s oldest peaceful uses.
clips.text: Liuyang. Liuyang has made fireworks for many centuries and is called the “home of fireworks” — one of gunpowder’s oldest peaceful uses.

clips.send: Ichisi. Today: Near Macon, Georgia. A chiefdom on the Ocmulgee River, probably centered at the Lamar mounds near Macon. De Soto’s army arrived in late March 1540 — the first Europeans its people had ever seen.
clips.text: Ichisi. Today: Near Macon, Georgia. A chiefdom on the Ocmulgee River, probably centered at the Lamar mounds near Macon. De Soto’s army arrived in late March 1540 — the first Europeans its people had ever seen.

clips.send: Dujiangyan. Today: Dujiangyan, Sichuan. The Fish Mouth splits the Min River in two, the Feisha Weir spills floods, and the Bottle-Neck Channel lets water onto the Chengdu Plain — still working after 2,200 years.
clips.text: Dujiangyan. Today: Dujiangyan, Sichuan. The Fish Mouth splits the Min River in two, the Feisha Weir spills floods, and the Bottle-Neck Channel lets water onto the Chengdu Plain — still working after 2,200 years.

clips.send: Zhenjiang. Canal boats crossed the Yangtze here, with Yangzhou on the far bank. The Jianbi ship lock still links the canal and the river today.
clips.text: Zhenjiang. Canal boats crossed the Yangtze here, with Yangzhou on the far bank. The Jianbi ship lock still links the canal and the river today.

clips.send: Fort Jackson. Today: Near Wetumpka, Alabama. After the Creek War, Andrew Jackson forced the 1814 Treaty of Fort Jackson here, taking about 23 million acres — even from Creek towns that had fought on his side. Today the site is Fort Toulouse–Fort Jackson Park, with rebuilt forts and a riverside arboretum.

clips.send: Cairo. Saladin built its Citadel on a hill in the 1170s. In the Middle Ages it was one of the biggest trading cities in the world.
clips.text: Cairo. Saladin built its Citadel on a hill in the 1170s. In the Middle Ages it was one of the biggest trading cities in the world.

clips.send: Fei River (Shouyang). Today: Shou County, Anhui. The Eastern Jin beat the much bigger Former Qin army here. Fleeing soldiers took every bush on Mount Bagong for an enemy.
clips.text: Fei River (Shouyang). Today: Shou County, Anhui. The Eastern Jin beat the much bigger Former Qin army here. Fleeing soldiers took every bush on Mount Bagong for an enemy.

clips.send: Providence. Roger Williams, banished from Massachusetts for his ideas, founded it in 1636 on land he got from the Narragansett people. He named it for God’s “providence” (care); today it is the capital of Rhode Island.
clips.text: Providence. Roger Williams, banished from Massachusetts for his ideas, founded it in 1636 on land he got from the Narragansett people. He named it for God’s “providence” (care); today it is the capital of Rhode Island.

clips.send: Federal Hall. On 30 April 1789 George Washington took the oath as the first President on a balcony here, when New York was the nation’s capital. Today’s building (1842) stands on the same spot on Wall Street, with a big statue of Washington on its steps.

clips.send: Yizhou. Today: Taiwan. In 230 Sun Quan sent Wei Wen with a fleet of ten thousand soldiers across the sea to Yizhou — the earliest record of mainland people reaching Taiwan in large numbers.
clips.text: Yizhou. Today: Taiwan. In 230 Sun Quan sent Wei Wen with a fleet of ten thousand soldiers across the sea to Yizhou — the earliest record of mainland people reaching Taiwan in large numbers.

clips.send: Appalachian Mountains. A 1,500-mile chain of very old, worn-down mountains that ends in north Georgia, where the Appalachian Trail starts at Springer Mountain. The Proclamation of 1763 banned colonists from settling west of them — one of the complaints that led to the Revolution.

clips.send: Shule (Kashgar). Today: Kashgar (Kashi), Xinjiang. The last big oasis before the Pamir mountains — caravans rested here before the hard climb west.
clips.text: Shule (Kashgar). Today: Kashgar (Kashi), Xinjiang. The last big oasis before the Pamir mountains — caravans rested here before the hard climb west.

clips.send: Zhaozhou Bridge. Today: Zhao County, Hebei. The world’s oldest surviving open-spandrel stone arch bridge: small arches on top of the big one let floodwater through and make it lighter.
clips.text: Zhaozhou Bridge. Today: Zhao County, Hebei. The world’s oldest surviving open-spandrel stone arch bridge: small arches on top of the big one let floodwater through and make it lighter.

clips.send: Matterhorn. A sharp pyramid-shaped peak (4,478 m) in the Alps on the Swiss–Italian border.
clips.text: Matterhorn. A sharp pyramid-shaped peak (4,478 m) in the Alps on the Swiss–Italian border.

clips.send: China–Laos Railway. 1,035 km from Kunming in China to Vientiane, capital of Laos, through 167 tunnels. It gives land-locked Laos a fast link to ports and markets.
clips.text: China–Laos Railway. 1,035 km from Kunming in China to Vientiane, capital of Laos, through 167 tunnels. It gives land-locked Laos a fast link to ports and markets.

clips.send: Hushan. Today: Dandong, Liaoning. On the Yalu River at the border with the DPRK (North Korea). The 2009 survey put the eastern start of the Ming Great Wall here.
clips.text: Hushan. Today: Dandong, Liaoning. On the Yalu River at the border with the DPRK (North Korea). The 2009 survey put the eastern start of the Ming Great Wall here.

clips.send: Babylon. Today: near Hillah, Iraq. Hammurabi ruled from here and set up his law code. Around 600 BCE it was the biggest city in the world, entered through the blue Ishtar Gate.
clips.text: Babylon. Today: near Hillah, Iraq. Hammurabi ruled from here and set up his law code. Around 600 BCE it was the biggest city in the world, entered through the blue Ishtar Gate.

clips.send: Tokyo Bay. On the deck of the battleship USS Missouri, Japan signed the Instrument of Surrender. China’s representative signed for the Allies too.
clips.text: Tokyo Bay. On the deck of the battleship USS Missouri, Japan signed the Instrument of Surrender. China’s representative signed for the Allies too.

clips.send: Yellowstone National Park. Today: Wyoming, USA. The world’s first national park (1872), famous for geysers and hot springs. At Mammoth Hot Springs, warm water builds terraces of travertine.
clips.text: Yellowstone National Park. Today: Wyoming, USA. The world’s first national park (1872), famous for geysers and hot springs. At Mammoth Hot Springs, warm water builds terraces of travertine.

clips.send: Trail of Tears State Park. In the bitter winter of 1838–39, Cherokee families on the forced removal waited for weeks to cross the ice-choked Mississippi River here. Many died of cold and sickness; the park in Missouri remembers them.
clips.text: Trail of Tears State Park. In the bitter winter of 1838–39, Cherokee families on the forced removal waited for weeks to cross the ice-choked Mississippi River here. Many died of cold and sickness; the park in Missouri remembers them.

clips.send: Wanning Bridge. The oldest bridge on the Central Axis. Under the Yuan, grain boats on the Grand Canal passed beneath it into Jishuitan — the canal’s northern end.
clips.text: Wanning Bridge. The oldest bridge on the Central Axis. Under the Yuan, grain boats on the Grand Canal passed beneath it into Jishuitan — the canal’s northern end.

clips.send: Bohai Kingdom. Today: Ning’an, Heilongjiang (capital Shangjing Longquanfu). The Tang made its ruler “King of Bohai”. Its capital was laid out like a small Chang’an.
clips.text: Bohai Kingdom. Today: Ning’an, Heilongjiang (capital Shangjing Longquanfu). The Tang made its ruler “King of Bohai”. Its capital was laid out like a small Chang’an.

clips.send: Gushan Island. Today: West Lake, Hangzhou. The biggest island in West Lake, a small hill joined to the shore by the Bai Causeway. The Tang temple is gone; today there are gardens and a museum.
clips.text: Gushan Island. Today: West Lake, Hangzhou. The biggest island in West Lake, a small hill joined to the shore by the Bai Causeway. The Tang temple is gone; today there are gardens and a museum.

clips.send: Jinzhou. Today: Jinzhou, Liaoning. Taking Jinzhou closed the “door” between Northeast China and North China, so the Nationalist armies there were trapped.
clips.text: Jinzhou. Today: Jinzhou, Liaoning. Taking Jinzhou closed the “door” between Northeast China and North China, so the Nationalist armies there were trapped.

clips.send: Independence Rock. A huge granite dome where emigrants carved or painted their names — more than 5,000 can still be found. Wagon trains tried to reach it by the Fourth of July so they would cross the mountains before the snow.
clips.text: Independence Rock. A huge granite dome where emigrants carved or painted their names — more than 5,000 can still be found. Wagon trains tried to reach it by the Fourth of July so they would cross the mountains before the snow.

clips.send: Five Streams. Today: western Hunan and eastern Guizhou. Five mountain streams that flow into the Yuan River. Crossing all five shows how far from home Wang Changling had to go.
clips.text: Five Streams. Today: western Hunan and eastern Guizhou. Five mountain streams that flow into the Yuan River. Crossing all five shows how far from home Wang Changling had to go.

clips.send: North Sea. A shallow, stormy part of the Atlantic between Britain, Norway, Denmark, Germany and the Netherlands, with oil and gas under its floor.
clips.text: North Sea. A shallow, stormy part of the Atlantic between Britain, Norway, Denmark, Germany and the Netherlands, with oil and gas under its floor.

clips.send: Torres del Paine. Granite towers in Patagonia, in the far south of Chile, near the cold southern tip of the Andes.
clips.text: Torres del Paine. Granite towers in Patagonia, in the far south of Chile, near the cold southern tip of the Andes.

clips.send: Bangkok. Capital of Thailand, on the delta of the Chao Phraya River, famous for its temples and canals.
clips.text: Bangkok. Capital of Thailand, on the delta of the Chao Phraya River, famous for its temples and canals.

clips.send: Kalinga. Today: Odisha, India (Dhauli hill). After conquering Kalinga, Ashoka was so sorry for the suffering that he turned to Buddhism and peace. His edicts are carved on a rock at Dhauli.
clips.text: Kalinga. Today: Odisha, India (Dhauli hill). After conquering Kalinga, Ashoka was so sorry for the suffering that he turned to Buddhism and peace. His edicts are carved on a rock at Dhauli.

clips.send: Independence Hall. The Declaration of Independence was signed here in 1776, and the Constitution was written here in the summer of 1787 — both in the same Assembly Room. George Washington’s “rising sun” chair still stands at the front of the room.
clips.text: Independence Hall. The Declaration of Independence was signed here in 1776, and the Constitution was written here in the summer of 1787 — both in the same Assembly Room. George Washington’s “rising sun” chair still stands at the front of the room.

clips.send: James River. In 1607 three English ships sailed up this river, named for King James I, and the colonists built Jamestown on its bank. Later, tobacco plantations worked by enslaved people lined its shores.
clips.text: James River. In 1607 three English ships sailed up this river, named for King James I, and the colonists built Jamestown on its bank. Later, tobacco plantations worked by enslaved people lined its shores.

clips.send: Blue Ridge Mountains. Part of the old, worn-down Appalachians. In north Georgia they hold the state’s highest point, Brasstown Bald (1,458 m).
clips.text: Blue Ridge Mountains. Part of the old, worn-down Appalachians. In north Georgia they hold the state’s highest point, Brasstown Bald (1,458 m).

clips.send: Pyrenees. A mountain wall about 430 km long between France and Spain. The tiny country of Andorra sits high in its valleys.
clips.text: Pyrenees. A mountain wall about 430 km long between France and Spain. The tiny country of Andorra sits high in its valleys.

clips.send: Northwest Territory. Today: Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, Wisconsin, part of Minnesota. The Northwest Ordinance of 1787 banned slavery here and promised that new states made from it would be equal to the old ones; five states came from it. The Shawnee, Miami and other nations fought hard to keep their lands but lost their British allies after the War of 1812.
